articleTitle: Demand Side Management and Economic Analysis Using Battery Storage System (BSS) and Solar Energy
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Shortage of power generation results in unplanned load shedding. Active participation of the people on the demand side provides a solution by moving loads from peak time to off/peak hours during the day. This paper presents a Demand Side Management (DSM) that includes a rooftop photovoltaic system, a Battery Storage System (BSS), a hybrid control system, and a grid-tie inverter to reduce peak demands. The hybrid controller ensures that the maximum solar power generated is used or stored in the batteries for a given load, and any excess energy feeds the power grid. In this system, essential loads and generated power from rooftop PV systems are constantly monitored, and power generated by solar panels is preferred above grid electricity. According to the results, this system provides 100 % of each residence’s required energy, plus an annual 6497 kWh to feed the AC grid and store in the BSS, resulting in monthly cost savings and the elimination of peak loads, particularly during the summer months, as well as a variety of environmental benefits.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Solar PV System for a University Building
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: System Advisor Model (SAM) software was used to analyze a grid-connected solar photovoltaic system on the rooftop of the Student Union Building (SUB) at Texas Tech University. The SUB has an average daily load requirement of 7917 kWh/day, and the average load per year is 2.89 GWh. A simulation of a PV system under various load circumstances was conducted. A 327 W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> monocrystalline silicon module was utilized to reach a total power of 141.6 kW, using a rooftop area of 2168 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The system can provide about 12 % of the required energy for the SUB, resulting in energy cost savings.

articleTitle: Long-Term Load Forecasting Based on Feature fusion and LightGBM
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Load forecasting is of great significance for the early planning of integrated energy system. However, for new buildings and old buildings without historical data, there is no historical load data, and the traditional load forecasting model is no longer applicable. Therefore, for this kind of buildings, based on load correlation analysis, this paper proposes a long-term load forecasting model based on feature fusion and LightGBM. After effective feature analysis of different types of features, this paper uses the method of feature fusion to construct the final input, and with the learning advantage of LightGBM model for regression problem. It uses histogram algorithm to discretize the data, speeds up the calculation, and uses gradient unilateral sampling algorithm to reduce the number of training samples in iteration and avoid over-fitting. We execute an experimental analysis on the load simulation dataset of 205 typical buildings, and finally evaluate the accuracy of the model through the parameters such as statistical metrics MSE, MAE and correlations coefficient. The experiment results show that compared with other algorithms, the proposed method has higher accuracy and faster speed, which is of great significance for the load forecasting of new and old buildings without historical data.

articleTitle: The Influence of Tilt Angle on Output for a Residential 4 kW Solar PV System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The tilt angle of a photovoltaic (PV) module has a significant impact on its energy generation capabilities. This study looks at the influence of monthly tilting versus fixed, one-axis, and two-axis tracking systems on the energy production of a small, residential 4 kW PV system in Texas. System Advisor Model (SAM) was used to simulate and compare each scenario. Just using a manual angle adjustable solar panel mount bracket (ASPVB) to adjust tilt can boost generated electricity by 6% when compared to a fixed rack system with a tilt equal to that of the local latitude.

articleTitle: Control Methods for a Bi-directional DC-DC Converter in Fuel Cell Hybrid Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This paper presents methods adapted for the control of a bi-directional DC-DC converter in fuel cell hybrid vehicle applications. To interconnect the high voltage battery to the DC bus, a cascaded hard-switched buck and boost converter is chosen to allow operation of the electric drive train with overlapping input and output voltages. Specifically, current, power and voltage control are investigated for the boost and buck modes based on dynamic averaging converter models. The design shows that using active compensation of the input and output voltages, the same controller settings can be used for both modes of converter operation, and in particular, these settings are specified independently of the load. Furthermore, the methods demonstrate that at constant current flow, control deviations are avoided by dynamically applying a correction to the control voltage during the transition from boost to buck mode and vice versa. A case study with representative voltage and power values for a fuel cell hybrid vehicle verifies the suggested methods by means of simulations.

articleTitle: Comparative Studies on Use of Discrete Wavelet Transform-based Feature Extraction for Peak Load Forecasting Using LSTM
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Peak load forecasting (PLF) is crucial for the power system operation to consider sufficient spinning reserve. Different machine learning algorithms such as Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) are widely used to conduct time-series forecasting. This paper proposes a method based on LSTM integrated with Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), which extracts features of power system peak loads, meteorological and calendar data. This paper presents a comparative analysis of the proposed method along with RNN and LSTM. Results show that the DWT-LSTM has a higher R2 and lower error metrics (Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE)) compared to the conventional methods. Comparative studies for DWT-LSTM considering various mother wavelets (Haar, Daubechies, biorthogonal and reverse biorthogonal) are also conducted. Simulation results show that Daubechies wavelet outperforms other mother wavelets. Besides, the filter length and decomposition level of DWT are also essential to conduct the feature extraction.

articleTitle: Dimensional and Numerical Analysis of Power Prediction of a Real-Scale Archimedes Spiral Wind Turbine Based on the Experimental Data of Small-Scaled Models
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Manufacturing a large-scale wind turbine is always a challenging task. Before sending the design for molding, some essential aerodynamics characteristics are needed to be learned. After a preliminary study on Archimedes spiral wind turbine, this paper aims to discuss the experimental data of two small-scale rotor blades with a diameter of 150 mm and 226 mm to estimate the characteristics of the real-scale wind turbine. Buckingham Pi theorem is applied to obtain the co-relation of torque and diameter of the turbine. This co-relation equation is used to estimate the characteristics of a real-scale Archimedes spiral wind turbine with a diameter of 1500 mm. Using this co-relation, approximate energy generated by the different field sizes of Archimedes spiral wind turbine with different tip speed ratios can be obtained. A computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation is done to compare the result of dimensional analysis.

articleTitle: Analysis of Cell-to-Cell Variation in a Battery Pack after Long Service Life Using Parameter Identification
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The characterization and monitoring of lithium-ion battery systems during their service life in electric or hybrid-electric powered vehicles is relevant from a safety perspective, but also for the purpose of further use or repatriation to the value chain. The condition estimation based on parameter identification of battery systems during usage offers insights to make decisions regarding to further use, recycling, but also maintenance. Due to variable environmental influences and load profiles, the cell behaviour can change over the service life. Accordingly, this paper presents a method which approximates the open-circuit voltage (OCV) based on rest phases recorded in real world drive cycles. By analysing identified cell voltage differences and therefore capacity differences, the method functions as an indicator for inhomogeneous aging behaviour in a battery pack. Hence, it is intended to provide information about the condition of the battery before it reaches the end of its service life without additional testing and thus about its potential for further use.

articleTitle: Adaptive Power Control of VSC-HVDC as a Corrective Measure
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This paper provides a novel control approach for Voltage Source Converter High Voltage Direct Current systems (VSC-HVDC) based on the voltage angles between the points of common coupling (PCC). The control aimed at an automatic relief of the parallel lines in case of disturbances as well as an increase of the transient stability. The basic principle of the control system and its integration into classic VSC-HVDC control concepts were described. An implementation of the voltage angle control (VAC) and the HVDC model for transient stability studies were presented. Simulations were carried out in a modified Nordic Test System with an additional HVDC integration, where the methods of using a droop-based AC-emulation control (ACE) and the VAC with PI-controllers were analyzed. Simulations showed that HVDC systems with Droop control (ACE) only take over a part of the failed power flow despite corresponding transmission reserve, whereas PI control (VAC) could take over the entire power flow. The HVDC systems could automatically compensate parallel lines in the event of a disturbance and improve power system stability.

articleTitle: Modeling and Implementation of Multiphase Switched-Capacitor Coupled-Inductor Converter
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The modeling and implementation of a closed-loop scheme of multiphase switched-capacitor coupled-inductor (MSCCI) converter is presented to achieve high-gain DC-DC step-up conversion/regulation. The MSCCI’s power part is a cascade structure from supply Vs to output Vo, including a three-stage switched-capacitor booster and a coupled inductor involved. The gain can be boosted to 4[n+1+(1+nD)/(1−D))] at most theoretically, where n is turn ratio of coupled inductor and D is the duty cycle of pulse-width modulation (PWM), e.g., max. of Vo reaches 44 times value of Vs while n=4, D=0.5. It is noteworthy that fewer components are just needed for this high gain with the help of multiphase operation. Further, the MSCCI’s modeling is derived, and the simulation/experiment cases are illustrated/verified on the prototype so as to present the efficacy of MSCCI’s scheme.

articleTitle: Design of a Single Inductor LED Sink Driver Employing a Negative Hybrid Cockcroft-Walton/Dickson Multiplier
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: For a lithium-ion battery input, a new LED (Light-Emitting Diode) sink driver with a single inductor is presented in this paper. Unlike existing LED sink drivers, the proposed driver consists of a negative hybrid Cockcroft-Walton/Dickson multiplier and a buck-boost converter. By connecting the negative hybrid Cockcroft-Walton/Dickson multiplier to the buck-boost converter in series, the proposed topology can provide not only a higher voltage gain but also smaller component count and simpler switching control. To confirm the effectiveness of the proposed topology, theoretical analysis, computer simulations and experiments were performed regarding the simplest proposed driver realizing 8 times gain. Furthermore, the comparative analysis clarified that the proposed driver can provide higher power efficiency and smaller component counts than conventional drivers.

articleTitle: Vibration Energy Harvesting Using a MISO Converter Employing Hybrid Cockcroft-Walton/Dickson Multipliers
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Vibration energy harvesting is the concept to convert vibrations in an electrical power. For the vibration energy harvesting, a multiple-input single-output (MISO) ac/dc converter is proposed in this paper. Unlike existing converters for vibration energy conversion, the proposed converter achieves not only inductor-less structure but also high voltage gains by the stack topology using hybrid Cockcroft-Walton/Dickson multipliers (HCWDMs). Regarding the proposed MISO converter with two modules, the characteristics, such as power efficiency and output voltage, are clarified by theoretical analysis and simulation program with integrated circuit emphasis (SPICE) simulations. Furthermore, the validity of the proposed MISO topology is confirmed by breadboard tests.

articleTitle: A MQTT-based Soil Moisture Level Notification System for a Smart Farm
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Smart irrigation is among the IoT smart farming practices deemed important in optimizing the ever-growing need for farm produce given the climate change and other farm produce affecting events e.g., COVID-19. In this paper we aim at enhancing the existing technology in smart farming by proposing some insight towards developing an easy-to-use tool. The tool helps irrigation farmers in making informed decisions on their water sprinkler placement for maintaining the recommended soil water moisture contents for their farm. Our framework notifies the farmer when the sprinklers rearrangement is due based on the farm’s soil moisture level readings. Our work defines the optimal computational parameter values for the strategic sprinkler deployment and introduces the required instruments and set up procedure. We demonstrate the implementation and user-friendly output of the apparatus with a display showing the actionable soil moisture information. Such results will provide the very critical information needed by a smart irrigation farmer to make informed decisions about their farm based on its soil water moisture contents.

articleTitle: On-line Detection Method of Supraharmonic in Distribution Network Based on Identification of Switching Frequency
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Supraharmonic is a new power quality problem with the development trend of power electronic distribution network. Existing studies suggest that supraharmonic is generated by the switching action of power electronic equipment, and the emission is mainly concentrated in the integral multiple of the switching frequency of power electronic equipment. The method of bandwidth aggregation near the switching frequency can better reflect the typical characteristics of supraharmonic. Based on the generation mechanism and distribution regularity of supraharmonic, this paper proposes an switching frequency identification method for on-line detection. According to the distribution characteristics of supraharmonic, this method can effectively extract the equipment switching frequency on-line and simplify the detection data, which lays the foundation for the further analysis and calculation of supraharmonic.

articleTitle: Power System Operation in the presence of Flexible Prosumers considering System Congestion
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In the daily operation of the power system, there are different ways to operate the system. Also, there would be disturbances that lead to congestion in the power system. The ability of the power system to respond to those disturbances, also called power system flexibility, is an important power system criterion. The first part of this paper assesses the power system performance under different objective functions using optimal power flow analysis. The second part of the paper studies the impact of using flexible loads and prosumers on the power system performance during congestion events by carrying out optimal power flow analysis. To obtain results, three power systems were used: the IEEE 5-bus system, the modified IEEE 5-bus system with flexible loads, the modified IEEE 5-bus system with Prosumers. It is found that an enhancement in performance took place after adding flexible loads and prosumers. Moreover, congestion is managed effectively in the presence of flexible loads and prosumers.

articleTitle: Optimal Hybrid Renewable Energy System Design for Generation Cost Reduction and Increased Electrification in Isolated Grid in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Remote areas in the Indonesia archipelago are mostly isolated from the utility grid and powered by expensively known diesel generators. Due to the limited access and transportation system, the diesel fuel price can be very high. Therefore, the power can only be served to 1.83% of the population, and worse, these customers are not even fully electrified in 24-hours. This research presents Hybrid Renewable Energy System (HRES) design in the isolated grids in Indonesia. The HRES consists of the existing diesel generators with the solar PV system and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). The optimized design of HRES is obtained following two objectives, such as the lowest generation cost and highest number of customers served. The HRES is implemented in one isolated grid in Indonesia, and the design is validated using HOMER software. The result shows that the implementation of HRES can reduce the generation cost by 50% and increase the electrification to 7.6%.

articleTitle: Analysis of Center of Inertial Frequency in a Power Grid that Includes Distributed Energy Resources Connected via Smart Inverters
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In recent years, the control function of grid-connected inverters called “smart inverters” has increased in sophistication, and the function of stabilization of the system frequency and terminal voltage is implemented. The stability of the entire system could be ensured if these high-performance grid-connected inverters are utilized efficiently. However, the control function of such an inverter generally differs across manufacturers, and the details are not disclosed. Therefore, in this study, a power system with grid-connected inverters and synchronous generator is considered for classifying these characteristics and establishing a grid code for each control type without depending on the method of implementing inverter control. The power system is analyzed, and its performance is indexed using the concept of “center of inertia frequency.”

articleTitle: Control Strategy Analysis of a Novel Transformerless Unified Power Quality Controller Based on Ultracapacitor and TRIAC
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Unified Power Quality Controller (UPQC) can deal with most kinds of power quality problems perfectly, yet its high economic cost hinders its large-scale promotion. Hence, this paper adopts a cost-effective transformerless UPQC based on ultracapacitor and triode for alternating current (TRIAC) with fewer IGBT modules to deal with voltage and current quality problems together. At first, the topologies of the traditional and improved UPQC are compared, and then the LCL and LC filters are designed to be effective for both voltage and current compensation considering the voltage drop and current control precision. Meanwhile, the inverter control strategies for both the uninterruptible power supply (UPS) and active power filter (APF) mode are designed with high dynamic performance and control accuracy, the series-connected ultracapacitor modules used as energy backup enhance the fault ride-through capability of the improved UPQC. Finally, offline simulations and controller hardware in the loop tests were carried out to verify the feasibility of the proposed control strategy of the improved UPQC.

articleTitle: Optimal Deployment Capacity of District Multi-Energy System Considering Cost Evolution
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: For the purpose of coping with the severe climate change challenge arising by greenhouse gas emission, a novel energy system paradigm, generally so-called District Multi-Energy System (DMES), has turned out to be the most influential solution for existing energy system to transit to a higher efficient, lower-carbon, safer and more sustainable energy environment. Hence, a large number of researches have already contributed to address optimal problems relevant to planning, deployment, operation, management in DMES area. In the context of these efforts, energy technology cost, a significantly important parameter in optimization target, is often assumed as a given value being irrelevant to optimal decision-making. Such an approach clearly neglects the evolutional characteristic of energy technology and consequently leads to less accurate optimization results. In this respect, integrating multiple types of energy carriers, in particular renewables, a kind of DMES model is proposed which intends to obtain the optimal deployment capacity of different power units involved in the energy system. Moreover, learning curve model that depicts the evolution trajectory of energy technology cost is also incorporated to DMES model to investigate the impact of cost evolution on optimal results.

articleTitle: Controller Chip Design of Coupled-Inductor Cockcroft-Walton-Switched-Capacitor Boost DC-AC Inverter
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of the controller chip applied to coupled-inductor Cockcroft-Walton-switched-capacitor (CICWSC) inverter for boost DC-AC conversion. In this inverter circuit, the plant is the power part of CICWSC, composed of CI booster, CWSC doubler, and halfbridge DC-link circuit, aiming at the step-up conversion from DC 24V to AC 100V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RMS</inf>, 60Hz. To achieve this target, the control part of CICWSC is made up of phase generator and sinusoidal pulse-width-modulation (SPWM) controller, and its integrated circuit is designed by using Cadence tool through pre-layout simulation and post-layout simulation. And then, with the help of Chip Design & Implementation Center, this controller is implemented on a real chip: no. D35-104B-E0013, TSMC 0.35μm 2P4M, 750×700μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 3.3V, 3.889mW, max freq. 100kHz, 18S/B. Further, the prototype circuit of CICWSC is achieved, and is also checked for experimental verification with some cases of boost DC-AC conversion.

articleTitle: Supraharmonic Emissions of a bidirectional electric vehicle charging station - a research methodology based on tests at reconstructed distribution grid
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Bidirectional electric vehicle charging stations (EVSE) offer new business models like Demand Response to users or can provide ancillary services to support the electrical grid (V2G and G2V). This type of charging station represents a novelty in the electrical grid, as it is considered as load and as power generation unit at the same time. In this study the supraharmonic emissions of a bidirectional EVSE are analyzed at a reconstructed electrical distribution grid. The emissions are determined according to existing standards (IEC61000-4-7 and IEC61000-4-30) for different grid conditions and operating points. Influence factors for supraharmonic emissions are identified as well as narrowband and wideband emissions of the EVSE. Time-domain analysis of the high-frequency signals which can lead to equipment malfunction concludes this work and emphasizes the need of regulations in this frequency range.

articleTitle: Battery Management Systems Topologies: Applications : Implications of different voltage levels
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: A safe and reliable battery management system (BMS) is a key component of a functional battery storage system. This paper focusses on the hardware requirements of BMS and their related topologies. It is briefly described which general requirements must be fulfilled to design a BMS for a given application. Several applications in different voltage classes, ranging from 60 volts to 1500 volts are presented. To give a practical overview, those applications are discussed and evaluated with a systemic, technical and economic perspective of the applied topology. The designer of a BMS is provided with practical information and guidance.

articleTitle: Electricity Tariff Simulation on The Largest Electric Power System in Indonesia Using The Time Of Use and Critical Peak Pricing Schemes Based on Revenue Neutrality
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The current dynamic tariff has become a trend in developing countries, especially in the electricity sector. Flat tariff on electricity costumers causes the cost of electricity to be less optimal. In Indonesia, the second highest costumer group after industry is residential customer, who has 37,6 % of total electrical energy consumption. So naturally the load curve tends to approach the curve of residential needs. In the Java Madura Bali system, the peak load of a residential customer occurs at the same time as the peak load on the system. If load shifting scheme of the electrical energy consumption of the residential customer can be applied, it will give a big impact on the system. The peak load is borne by the power plants which generally have expensive operational costs. By the reduction of peak load using load shifting scheme, a significant increase of system efficiency will be obtained. This paper develops a method of determination of a dynamic tariff combination scheme, Time of Use (TOU) and Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) based on revenue neutrality. The scheme is simulated to residential customers in the Java Bali Madura system. From several scenarios, the results of the implementation of this scheme show the increasing of the total cost efficiency of electricity supply in the Java Madura Bali system.

articleTitle: Distributing the Generation of Electricity to Extreme Level
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Energy harvesting is the process of converting low level ambient energy into electrical energy usually in the μW to mW range. Energy harvesting enables the distribution of the production of electricity to extremely localized in situ electricity generation. This paper briefly describes our research work and results in the field of energy harvesting. Energy harvesting in general is first shortly discussed and then the design, implementation and testing of our inductive harvester are presented.

articleTitle: Application of Oil-immersed Transformer Fault Diagnosis Based on Modified Neural Network Combined with PSO
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Transformer fault diagnosis is a non-linear pattern recognition process. A single BP neural network has a slow convergence speed and is easy to fall into a local minimum. In this paper, based on the gas characteristics and fault types of oil-immersed transformers, a method is proposed on account of the dissolved gas analysis technology in transformer oil. A modified the transformer fault diagnosis algorithm of particle swarm optimization with neural network is suggested. By dynamically adjusting the inertia weight and acceleration factor of the PSO algorithm; by optimizing the standard particle swarm algorithm, an adaptive PSO-BP neural network transformer fault diagnosis system is established. The new and modified algorithm is used to establish a fault diagnosis model, and more than 300 samples are used for actual fault diagnosis, with an accuracy rate of over 94%. The results show that the modified PSO-BP is more accurate and reliable.

articleTitle: Drone-based sensing and exploration of overhead electric power lines
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: We propose a drone-based SWIM (Sequential Wave Imprinting Machine) approach to the sensing of overhead electric power lines. This will be useful in smart city sensing, e.g. to sense electric field distributions around overhead power lines without the need to stop traffic on the road as is often done with a bucket truck or lift truck that hoists utility workers up to the wires. Moreover, our remote sensing approach provides additional safety.

articleTitle: State Estimation in Large, Unbalanced Distribution Systems and its Applications on Network Reconfiguration and Demand Estimation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE 4th International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: State estimation in power systems refers to the problem of evaluating voltage magnitudes and angles at all nodes given a set of measurements. The application of state estimation in transmission systems, where the assumption of balanced network and loads is customary, has already reached a mature stage of development. However, the same is not true for distribution systems, owing to a number of reasons: (i) the need for a three-phase representation, since neither loads nor network are balanced, (ii) the usually large number of nodes, much larger than the number of nodes in transmission systems, which have a considerable impact on the stability of the numerical solution, and (iii) the fact that redundancy is not normally guaranteed. This paper then represents an attempt to deal with the state estimation problem in large, unbalanced distribution systems considering two main applications: load demand estimation and automatic network reconfiguration through a self-healing approach.
